text:
laura.dev: hey, quick help — we've got traces for incoming API requests but child spans from our background worker (python/celery) are missing. traces show only the root. anyone seen this with opentelemetry + celery?

mike_sre: saw this before when context propagation didn't make it into the worker. are you using W3C tracecontext headers (traceparent) when enqueuing?

laura.dev: we enqueue via requests to our task API; celery message broker is rabbitmq. we don't explicitly pass headers in the task call (using celery.send_task). the worker is instrumented with opentelemetry-instrumentation-celery and otel sdk v1.19.0.

nina.eng: two quick checks: 1) ensure celery instrumentation is applied in the worker process (import happens before app.start). 2) check that message attributes include traceparent — Celery needs broker headers forwarded.

laura.dev: how do I inspect the raw message headers in rabbit?

mike_sre: you can dump with rabbitmqctl or use the management UI -> Queues -> Get messages (requeue=false) to peek headers. look for "traceparent" or "tracecontext" key.

laura.dev: peeked — I see a header named "traceparent" on producer side, but on the worker-consumed message it's gone. so likely broker stripping or celery not copying.

observability.bot: FYI — our OTLP collector logs show intermittent "received span without parent" for service=worker-prod over the last 24h. trace_id present but parent_id null.

nina.eng: two action items: (A) enable DEBUG logs for opentelemetry.instrumentation.celery and opentelemetry.sdk.trace to confirm propagation, (B) try manual propagation helper when sending task:

laura.dev: example?

nina.eng: quick snippet — in producer side before calling task:

```python
from opentelemetry.propagate import inject
carrier = {}
inject(carrier)
# pass carrier as headers when sending
app.send_task('my.task', args=[...], headers=carrier)
```

nina.eng: and in worker ensure instrumentation picks up headers (instrumentation must wrap celery app init). also check runtime env: OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext should be set (we default to it).

mike_sre: also confirm broker version and any broker-plugins that sanitize headers. rabbit's content_type/content_encoding interplay can drop non-standard headers if messages get re-serialized.

laura.dev: made the change to pass headers explicitly and restarted worker, will test. any tips to validate end-to-end quickly?

observability.bot: quick debug flow: 1) make request with curl setting traceparent header: curl -H "traceparent: {your-value}" http://api/... 2) note trace id, 3) force enqueue, 4) search traces UI (Grafana Tempo) for trace id. dashboards: https://grafana.internal.redwood.com/d/observability/traces-overview and Tempo UI link https://tempo.internal.redwood.com/search

laura.dev: tried with manual header -> I can now see child spans for some tasks but not all. sampling? we're using ParentBasedTraceIdRatio with 0.1 probability in prod. could sampling explain partial visibility?

mike_sre: yes, if root is sampled false then children won't be exported. ParentBased sampler respects parent sampled flag. If you're generating traceparent on producer side without sampled bit set, you can force sampled in the header (for testing) by setting the sampled flag in traceparent.

nina.eng: for longer-term: adjust sampling or set the SDK to remote_sampler that respects our backend decisions, or change parent-based probability. For debugging, set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on locally.

laura.dev: thanks. one last oddity — some async tasks kicked off inside an async threadpool (concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor) and child spans from inside the thread pool are absent. any known asyncio/contextvars cases?

mike_sre: threading + contextvars can drop context. for threads you need to use attachotelcontext or manually copy contextvars into the thread. Example:

```python
from contextvars import copy_context
def submit(fn, *args):
    ctx = copy_context()
    def wrapped():
        return ctx.run(fn, *args)
    executor.submit(wrapped)
```

laura.dev: that fixed it for threadpool cases, thanks. will follow up with a small runbook and a PR to add header forwarding in the task producer.

nina.eng: great — also add a tiny dashboard query to surface "spans with no parent" per service so we can catch regressions (Grafana panel: count_over_time({service="worker-prod"} |= "received span without parent"[1h])).

laura.dev: noted. will ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:
